objective: Prove which self-blind contact laws u(in, out) + v(in, out) tell a contact's two rings apart (re-routing at the contact changes the automaton): exactly those nonlinear in a ring's two neighbours or reading the arriving cells unequally; that on one-way rings an affine law that sees the routing leaves one ring's arriving corner a dead end; and that under affine laws binding (A32) is dependence on both rings.
status: Proved 2026-11-09: among the 256 self-blind contact laws u(l_a, r_a) + v(l_b, r_b) on rule-60 rings, re-routing at a contact changes the automaton exactly unless u and v are affine with equal arriving-cell coefficients (32 blind laws, law (12,12) among them); an affine law that sees the routing reads only one arriving cell, cutting the other ring there, so a law that sees the routing with both rings passing is nonlinear; and binding is needing under affine laws, stronger under nonlinear ones.
title: Which contact laws see how rings continue
